If your flat is in Lagos State and governed by the Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, the law sets rules on how a landlord may lawfully recover possession. A notice to quit ends the tenancy but does not give the landlord the right to lock you out. If you stayed after the notice expired, the landlord must serve a written notice of intention to recover possession giving at least seven days' notice, and only after that can the landlord apply to court.

If your tenancy agreement is silent on notice, the minimum notice your landlord must give depends on your tenancy type: a tenant at will gets one week's notice, a monthly tenant gets one month's notice, a quarterly tenant gets three months' notice, a half-yearly tenant gets three months' notice, and a yearly tenant gets six months' notice. If your agreement does set a notice period, that agreed period normally applies.

Most residential tenancies in Lagos State are governed by the Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, which sets rules on how a landlord may lawfully recover possession. A notice to quit ends the tenancy but does not give the landlord the right to lock the tenant out. Under the law, if the tenant stays after the notice to quit expires, the landlord must serve a written notice of the owner's intention to recover possession, giving at least seven days' notice, and only after that can the landlord apply to court.
